title: U.S. House · Oklahoma's 4th District
area: South-central Oklahoma, including Norman, Lawton and Ada

candidates.name: Tom Cole

summary.text: Tom Cole is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for Oklahoma's 4th District, seeking re-election. A former history instructor and political consultant, he held Republican Party and state government posts in Oklahoma, including state senator and Secretary of State, before his 2002 election to Congress. He chairs the House Appropriations Committee and is an enrolled member of the Chickasaw Nation.

background.text: Born April 28, 1949, in Shreveport, Louisiana; his official biography describes him as a fifth-generation Oklahoman whose family returned to Oklahoma during his childhood, and his father served 20 years in the U.S. Air Force.
Holds a B.A. from Grinnell College, an M.A. from Yale University and a Ph.D. from the University of Oklahoma, and was a Thomas Watson Fellow and a Fulbright Fellow at the University of London.
Worked as a college instructor in history and politics, and is a founding partner and past president of CHS & Associates, an Oklahoma City political consulting and survey research firm.
Early political career: district director to U.S. Rep. Mickey Edwards, chairman of the Oklahoma Republican Party, and a member of the Oklahoma State Senate.
Served as Oklahoma's Secretary of State under Gov. Frank Keating from 1995 to 1999, including leading the state's effort to secure federal funds for rebuilding after the 1995 Oklahoma City bombing.

Was executive director of the National Republican Congressional Committee in the 1992 cycle, chief of staff of the Republican National Committee in the 2000 cycle, and chairman of the National Republican Congressional Committee in the 2008 cycle.
First elected to the U.S. House in 2002 and has represented Oklahoma's 4th District since 2003.
Has served on the House Appropriations Committee since 2009 and chairs it; previously chaired the House Rules Committee and served as a Republican Deputy Whip.

Is an enrolled member of the Chickasaw Nation and has been Republican co-chair of the Congressional Native American Caucus since 2009; according to his official biography, he lives in Moore, Oklahoma, with his wife, Ellen.

record.text: Voted in favor of the Water Resources Development Act of 2026.
Introduced companion legislation supporting the Miami Tribe of Oklahoma, which passed the U.S. House and was sent to the White House.
Introduced a resolution congratulating the University of Oklahoma baseball team for winning the 2026 Men's College World Series.

candidates.researchNotes: Key floor votes and FEC finance totals are added separately. Ballotpedia's page for Cole had little biographical content, so his biography draws on his official House biography and Wikipedia; record items are drawn from his official House press releases.

candidates.name: Mitchell Jacob

summary.text: Mitchell Jacob is the Democratic nominee in Oklahoma's 4th District. A Tulsa native and U.S. Army veteran who served as a Sergeant and Cryptologic Linguist, he earned a law degree from the University of Oklahoma in 2025 and works as a public defender. He ran for the Oklahoma House of Representatives in 2024 and says he is running on fiscal responsibility, public education and criminal justice reform.

background.text: Born in Tulsa, Oklahoma, and describes himself as a fourth-generation Oklahoman.

Earned a high school diploma from Boulder Creek High School, an associate degree from Rio Salado College (2016), a bachelor's degree from Grand Canyon University (2019), and a law degree from the University of Oklahoma College of Law (2025).
Served in the U.S. Army from 2017 to 2022 as a Sergeant and Cryptologic Linguist, deploying to southern Syria in support of Operation Inherent Resolve.
Career experience includes working as a stockbroker, banker, mortgage loan originator, and public defender.
Was the Democratic candidate for Oklahoma House of Representatives District 20 in 2024, losing to Republican Jonathan Wilk, 75.8% to 24.2%.
Says he is a father of five and lives in Newcastle, Oklahoma, with his wife and children.

priorities.text: Says the rapidly growing federal deficit and national debt is the biggest threat facing the country, and calls for spending cuts and reduced tax expenditures.
priorities.quote: The biggest threat to our democracy is our skyrocketing national debt. … We need to stop raising the debt limit, cut spending, greatly reduce our tax expenditures, and eliminate the federal debt.

priorities.text: Advocates for quality public education, small businesses, job creation, livable wages and human rights.
As a public defender, prioritizes criminal justice reform centered on rehabilitation over punishment.
priorities.quote: I believe that the first pillar of criminal justice is rehabilitation, and then it is punishment.

positions.summary: States that healthcare is a human right.
positions.quote: I believe that healthcare is a human right, and you should not have to work three jobs to get by.

positions.summary: Lists livable wages among his campaign priorities, alongside public education, small businesses and job creation.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website located in this research; positions and biography are drawn from his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey and profile.
